text:
sophia: Quick q about smokehouse delegation wiring — do we want the bench-prober service to own sampling logic (stratified/priority) or should intake publish sampling tags and let prober just execute? wondering about ownership boundaries and telemetry.
mike: my vote is sampling in intake. bench-prober should be stateless executor. simpler to reason about failures.
lara: +1 for intake owning it. we already tag traffic for A/B tests there. avoids double-decisions and duplicate sampling code.
jake: downside: intake needs tighter contract surface to convey sample metadata and golden artifacts. we need a clear proto for "SampleDescriptor" — fields: seed, heuristics, priority, origin
sophia: agree about descriptor. sketch:
SampleDescriptor { id: string; seed: int; strategy: enum{stratified, random, priority}; heuristics: list[string]; origin: enum{ingest, canary, manual} }
marco: what about telemetry? if intake selects, does it emit selection metrics or bench-prober? we want precise latency attribution.
mike: intake emits selection events (sample.selected) with descriptor. bench-prober emits execution events (prober.run, prober.latency) with descriptor id attached. join in telemetry pipeline.
lara: this keeps single source-of-truth for selection and simpler correlation downstream. we can compute selection->run latency.
sophia: tradeoffs — intake owning sampling means heavier ingest path and more coupling to sampling heuristics. bench-prober owning sampling reduces ingest work but increases runtime nondeterminism and duplicate heuristics across regions.
jake: also consider retries and idempotency. if bench-prober pulls samples on demand, it needs to respect the same golden selection guarantees; risk of off-by-one causing drift in experiments.
marco: long-term: maybe we standardize a small "sampling service" that both intake and bench-prober call. but that's a bigger refactor.
mike: agreed. for now, intake-owned sampling + small descriptor proto seems lowest risk.
sophia: ok action items: - jake: draft SampleDescriptor proto and add to model-intake contract (due EOD Thu); - lara: add selection telemetry events to intake emitters (PR by Mon); - marco: update bench-prober to join on descriptor.id for correlation (estimate 2d); - mike: add unit tests for selection->run join and a smoke telemetry dashboard.
jake: quick question — persist descriptor? or ephemeral only via event stream?
lara: persist minimal record (id, model_id, timestamp, strategy) for 7d. helps replays and debugging.
marco: +1 on 7d. keeps storage cheap and useful.
sophia: one more: inbound contract should include an optional `preferred_runner` hint so intake can bias selection for dedicated vs hosted pools.
mike: nice. that helps routing and cost control.
jake: i'll include preferred_runner in proto as optional string.
sophia: thanks all. pinging @eng-sre for infra considerations before we land the proto.
eng-sre-bot: Heads up — proto change will require schema migration plan. Please open change ticket and link migration runbook. :gear:
mike: will open ticket and tag infra team.
sophia: closing — we'll implement intake-owned sampling with descriptor proto and short persistence window. follow-ups on PRs in this thread. :thumbsup:
